# kama

> A C-family language (C#-like syntax, no garbage collector / RAII, explicit named
> parameters) that transpiles to portable C — running natively everywhere and in the browser
> via WebAssembly, with no runtime beside the compiled binary. MIT licensed.

kama's grammar is the source of truth: the compiler is a Flex lexer + Bison grammar + an
AST → C emitter. The docs below are generated from, or point at, that source so they don't
drift. For authoritative syntax read the grammar; for semantics read the spec; for runnable
examples read the test fixtures.

## Language
- [Tour](docs/tour.md): the guided introduction — the whole language in one read, every
  snippet compiled. Start here if you are new.
- [Specification](docs/SPEC.md): the full language reference — types, the
  `value`/`resource`/`contract` ownership model, generics, sum types + `match`, operators,
  smart pointers, collections, concurrency, FFI, build/debug. Start here for semantics.
- [Type model](docs/TYPE_MODEL.md): the ownership vocabulary in depth — `value` copies,
  `resource` moves, `contract` is the guarantee; the `type` marker + access-control rules.
- [Grammar (BNF)](docs/grammar.bnf): authoritative syntax, generated from `kama.y` by
  `tools/gen-grammar`.
- [Keyword reference](docs/KEYWORDS.md): every reserved word and what it does.
- [Coming from another language](docs/coming-from-other-languages.md): where kama's instincts differ from
  C#/Rust/Python and WHY — the rules an assistant trained on those languages will otherwise trip over
  (bind-to-a-local inference, private `resource` fields, `out` vs `ref`, `@generate` field marking,
  `.` constructs / `::` resolves scope). Every snippet is compiled by `tests/idioms_kama_way.kama`.
- [Goals & design philosophy](docs/GOALS.md): no-GC, one-way/simplicity, explicit>implicit,
  self-describing, LLM-discoverable.

## Examples
- [tests/](tests/): each `*.kama` is a runnable program with a `.expect` exit code.
  Representative fixtures: `type_kinds.kama` (value/resource/contract), `match_plain_enum.kama`
  and `optional_basic.kama` (sum types + `match`), `generic_fn_explicit.kama` (generics +
  turbofish), `math_lib.kama` (operator overloading + generic math), `owned_basic.kama` /
  `shared_iface.kama` (smart pointers), `dtor_block.kama` (RAII), `named_args.kama`,
  `refparam.kama` (ref/out), `ffi_struct.kama` (C interop).

## Toolchain & runtime
- [README](README.md): build/run via the containerized toolchain (`tools/cdev`); native +
  wasm targets; `kama build [--release] [--target <name-or-triple>]`.
- [Targets & toolchains](docs/targets.md): which platforms `--target` reaches, how to get a cross
  toolchain (your own / clang+sysroot / zig), output kinds, and per-platform notes.
- [Packages & projects](docs/packages.md): the `kama.json` manifest, dependencies, the lockfile,
  publishing, and the toolchain version manager.
- [Editor setup](docs/editors.md): `kama lsp` is a JSON-RPC/stdio language server built into the
  compiler — one server, thin clients. Config for VS Code, Neovim, Vim, Emacs, Sublime, Helix, Kate,
  plus which editors get syntax colour from what.
- [Runtime header](kama_runtime.h): the small C runtime included by generated code.
- [Repo guide for AI assistants](AGENTS.md): working conventions and build commands.

## For AI agents
- [Agent guide](docs/agents.md): **start here if you are an agent.** `kama query` answers from what
  the compiler RESOLVED rather than what a grep guessed — `--search NAME` finds a symbol by name
  across a package, `--complete` gives real signatures with parameter names, and `--json` wraps every
  mode in one envelope. Also: why `kama build`, not `kama check`, is the type check.
- `kama agents install` writes an `AGENTS.md` into a project (plus `--claude` / `--all-tools`
  pointers for tools that read something else). `kama agents print` emits it to stdout.

## Status
The **language feature set is complete** (see `VERSION`; on the road to 1.0). Implemented:
functions, primitives, control flow, named-parameter calls, `ref`/`out`; the **ownership type
model** (every declaration is `type value` / `type resource` / `type contract`); **RAII**
destruction (no GC); single inheritance + **virtual dispatch**; **contracts** (interfaces via
fat-pointer vtables); **enums and tagged unions** with value-producing, exhaustive **`match`**
(there is no `switch`); **`Optional<T>`/`Result<T,E>`** as the no-exceptions, no-`null` error
model; **generics** (monomorphized — user types + functions, contract bounds, `This`, explicit
turbofish `f::<T>()`); **operator overloading** + full static methods; the full
**smart-pointer family** (`Owned`/`Shared`/`Weak`) with auto-deref and custom allocators;
**collections** (`FixedArray`/`DynamicArray`/`InlineArray`/`Map`/`Set`/`Deque`/`PriorityQueue`/
sorted containers/`View<T>`/`string`, bounds-checked + RAII); the **`give`/`copy`** by-value
ownership model with compile-time use-after-move checking; **`const`-correctness**; **access
control** (private-by-default, `public`/`protected`/`friend`); **namespaces** + multi-file
builds; **C FFI** (`extern`, `Ptr`, raw memory confined to an explicit `unsafe { }` block);
**function pointers** (`fnptr`, `Type::method`, `BindableFunctionPtr`); **string interpolation**
+ format specifiers; **serialization** (`@generate`, by-value + object graph + polymorphic);
**shared-nothing concurrency** (isolates, typed channels, structured `scope`, `Atomic<T>`,
immutable `Shared`, `parallel_for` — no `async` colouring); **compile-time evaluation**
(`comptime` constants and `comptime fn`); **conditional compilation** (`@compileFor`); and the
**MCU surface** (`hardware` MMIO, `@interrupt`/`@section`/`@noheap`, inline `asm`, fallible
allocation). Targets **native, WebAssembly and bare-metal**, debug/release, with source-level
breakpoint debugging in an IDE and in browser DevTools. Tooling: a package + toolchain manager
(`kama pkg`, `kama toolchain`, `kama publish`) and a language server (`kama lsp`) serving eight
editors.

The remaining work before the 1.0 tag is documentation and release polish, not language
features — see [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md).
